question: 2017 Civic, grinding brakes when I stop. Any recall?

answer.text:
Short answer: NHTSA has no brake recall for the 2017 Civic.

NHTSA lists 6 recalls for the 2017 Civic, but none of them are for the brakes. They cover the power steering (18V663000), the fuel pump (23V858000), the front passenger seat weight sensor (26V332000), the right halfshaft on sedans and coupes (17V706000), and two that only affect hatchbacks and the Type R (18V266000 and 18V817000). Some of these depend on your body style, so I can't say which ones apply to your car yet. If you send me your VIN, I can narrow it down. You can also check your car's official recall status at nhtsa.gov/recalls with your VIN.

Owners have filed 38 brake-related complaints with NHTSA for this model year. These are unverified reports, not recalls, and none of them confirm a defect.

About the grinding: I'm not a mechanic, but common causes are brake pads worn down to the metal, worn or scored rotors, a stuck caliper, or a small stone caught behind the brake. Please have your brakes checked soon. Grinding often means metal is rubbing on metal, and that can make stopping less safe.

If it turns out you need new pads or rotors, tell me your body style (sedan, coupe or hatchback) or send your VIN, and I'll find parts that fit.
